_note: Phase 4 of docs/premium-skincare-brief.md — [PREMIUM-SKIN]. Entry-economics claims from documents ACTUALLY FETCHED on 2026-08-10. Two caveats bind every row here. (1) The Korean ODM cost and MOQ figures come from sourcing-agency marketing pages: they have a commercial interest in the numbers looking approachable, publish no methodology, and cannot be audited — LOW under CLAUDE.md's rubric, used only because two independent agencies quote overlapping ranges. (2) The customs figures come from a page whose most recent entry is dated 02-Feb-2018, so they are recorded as a stale MFN reference, not as a current 2026 rate. Modelled outputs (contribution margins, landed COGS, break-even discounts, cash at risk) are NOT here — they are computed by lib/transforms/premium_skin_entry.py from these inputs and live in data/manual/analysis/premium_skin_unit_economics.json, because a model output ledgered as a DataPoint would read as a measurement. Band retention statistics from the 2026-08-10 price re-sweep are also not here: they are SKU-population statistics produced by lib/transforms/premium_skin_band.py, which ledgers them itself.

claims.source_name: Storyboard18, reporting Honasa Consumer (Mamaearth) FY25 results
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] Honasa Consumer FY25 advertising spend Rs743.65cr (FY24 Rs661.28cr, +12.5%) against FY25 revenue Rs2,067cr (FY24 Rs1,919cr, +7.66%) = 36% of revenue. PAT fell 34.24% to Rs72.6cr from Rs110cr. Underlying volume growth 13.2%. ORGANISED, listed company, NET_REALISATION revenue basis. Used in Phase 4 as a FLOOR benchmark for customer acquisition cost, not a target: a scaled Indian beauty company with an established brand portfolio spends 36 paise of every revenue rupee on advertising. Basis mismatch stated deliberately — this is an advertising-to-revenue ratio for a mass-market portfolio, not a CAC for premium single-SKU trial. Trade press reporting a listed company's disclosed results, hence MEDIUM rather than HIGH; not read off the annual report itself.

claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] EX-WORKS factory cost per unit for a Korean-manufactured facial SERUM with PREMIUM actives, quoted range USD5.00-12.00; midpoint 8.50 recorded. claims.source_name: OEMKorea, 'Korean OEM Pricing Explained: What Drives Per-Unit Cost'
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] SPF TESTING cost per formula, quoted USD5,000-15,000; midpoint 10,000 recorded. A NON-RECURRING per-formula cost, not a per-unit cost — recorded here because it is the single largest one-off in a Korean-sourced launch and it falls entirely on the sunscreen SKU. At a 1,000-unit order it is USD5-15 a unit on a product whose whole ex-works cost is USD3-9, making the sunscreen's non-recurring cost roughly 2.7x its goods cost. It is the reason the sunscreen hero cannot be launched at the same order size as the serum. Same page also quotes patch testing USD1,500-3,500 per product. LOW confidence — sourcing-agency marketing content.

claims.source_name: OEMKorea, 'Korean OEM Pricing Explained: What Drives Per-Unit Cost'
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] VOLUME discount on ex-works unit cost, NOT a retail discount: per-unit cost falls 20-40% moving from a 1,000-unit order to a 5,000-unit order, then a further 10-20% from 5,000 to 10,000. Midpoint 30% recorded. metric discount_depth is used because it is a discount off a list cost; it is a SUPPLY-side figure and must never be read alongside the retail discount_depth points from the price sweeps, which measure platform discounting off MRP. This is the largest controllable lever on landed cost in the Phase 4 model and the reason a 4-SKU-at-MOQ launch shape fails. LOW confidence — sourcing-agency marketing content.

claims.source_name: EximGuru, Indian customs duty for tariff item 33049910 (face creams)
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] BASIC CUSTOMS DUTY on Indian tariff item 33049910, assessed on CIF value. STALE AND RECORDED AS SUCH: the page's most recent entry is dated 02-Feb-2018, when BCD was raised from 10% to 20%. NOT verified against a current CBIC notification, so it is a 2018 MFN reference rate, not a confirmed 2026 rate. Same page gives Social Welfare Surcharge 10% (levied on the BCD itself, so ~2% of CIF) and IGST 18%. IGST is CREDITABLE and is working capital, not margin — only BCD and SWS stick to a P&L. period recorded as 2018 rather than 2026 precisely so this is not read as current. The India-Korea CEPA may reduce this to zero for Korean-origin goods against a Form AK certificate of origin, but no page stating a preferential rate for HS 3304 could be fetched and verified, so Phase 4 models both 0% and 20% rather than assuming either.

claims.source_name: EximGuru, Indian customs duty for tariff item 33049910 (face creams)
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] IGST at import on tariff item 33049910, which also implies the domestic GST rate on the good. CREDITABLE input tax — affects working capital, never margin, and Phase 4's model excludes it from the P&L and reports it separately. Same staleness caveat as the BCD row: the page's most recent entry is 02-Feb-2018, and this has NOT been re-verified against the September-2025 GST slab restructure. A slab move would change every revenue line in the Phase 4 model, because India's MRP is GST-inclusive and revenue is MRP/(1+GST). Flagged in the model's assumptions block as an unverified input.
